full_script:
Sunday, shortly before noon. A modest residential bus stop, broad pavement and low apartment buildings. Taeo and Nib walk away from the stopped bus together, both already safely on the pavement. Taeo carries a plain small grocery bag in his LEFT hand; phone pocketed. Nib looks back once at the bus as its doors close, interested in the unfamiliar vehicle without a transport lesson.

A municipal gate-evacuation direction marker is part of the street furniture, small and unremarked, with a simple arrow and gate pictogram; no readable rule text or active gate. Ordinary pedestrians continue their own Sunday.

CAPTION: Sunday.

At the grandparents' closed front door. Taeo stops with his free hand near the doorbell, straightens the bag's twisted handle instead, then rings.

NIB: You're late?

TAEO: No.

Nib looks at the hand that hesitated. He does not diagnose the family relationship.

The door opens. The sibling's face brightens at Taeo before their gaze drops to Nib. The smile changes into plain surprise. Preserve the actual Chapter 1 sibling model.

SIBLING: You came.

TAEO: I said I would.

SIBLING: You say that a lot.

Not cruel, not a tearful accusation. Taeo has no quick answer.

The sibling notices the bag at Taeo's side. Taeo raises it slightly rather than offering it as an apology.

TAEO: Spicy ones.

SIBLING: Good.

Then, looking directly down at the visitor:

SIBLING: Who's this?

Nib stands beside Taeo, outside the threshold and unhidden.

NIB: Nib.

The sibling's hand stops on the door handle. Grandmother approaches from inside, drying her hands on a plain dish towel.

GRANDMOTHER: Let them in. The food's nearly ready.

Her expectation comes from Friday's call; the sibling's surprise establishes they were not silently briefed. One speaking-surprise beat is enough.

dialogue.text: Let them in. The food's nearly ready.

full_script:
Entry wide, with a clear route into the main room. Taeo takes off his own shoes at the sunken entry ledge. Nib waits on the entry side, then steps onto the raised indoor floor himself. Nobody picks him up or gives him a child's slippers.

TAEO: I told Grandma on Friday. I awakened this week.

SIBLING: You told Grandma Friday?

The sibling looks at Taeo, no longer at Nib. They mean the withheld news.

dialogue.text: I told Grandma on Friday. I awakened this week.

full_script:
From the main room, Grandfather has turned from the television toward the entry. He lowers the remote into his lap. Taeo has stepped inside with the bag; Nib follows one pace behind, not hidden by his legs.

GRANDFATHER: You awakened?

TAEO: I'll tell you.

GRANDFATHER: Come sit, then.

No automatic assumption that Grandfather already knows, no repeated question about speech.

Compact settling transition. Taeo transfers his phone from the jacket to his hoodie pocket, hangs his navy jacket on an entry wall hook, and sets the grocery bag beside the kitchen counter, on the floor and clear of feet. His black hoodie remains worn. The sibling pulls a thin puzzle board out just far enough from its storage beside the low cabinet to show him, keeping it supported flat.

SIBLING: I kept it.

TAEO: You haven't finished?

SIBLING: You said we'd do the sky together.

The specific previous shared activity is new ordinary family history, not a hidden present-week milestone. No flashback required.

dialogue.text: You said we'd do the sky together.

full_script:
Taeo crouches beside the board. A ragged gap cuts through its long pale cloud. Loose blue-and-white pieces are contained in a shallow sorting tray at its edge. He touches the board's rim, not a precarious loose piece.

TAEO: After we eat?

SIBLING: Today.

TAEO: Today.

Grandmother calls them from the meal table, off panel. The board slides back flat into its safe space for lunch.

Shared room/table anchor. Everyone is seated on floor cushions around the low rectangular table. Five ordinary settings; grilled fish in a central oval platter, side dishes, individual rice bowls, water cups. Nib sits at the east short end, normal full-size bowl within reach; nobody serves him on a pet dish or booster. Taeo sits at the south long side near Nib; sibling beside Taeo farther west. Grandmother sits north near the kitchen; Grandfather at the west short end. Window east, kitchen north, entry southwest. Keep this map in all meal shots.

Grandmother places her towel on the nearby kitchen counter after setting down the last dish, then sits. Grandfather has turned the TV off; its dark screen lies west. No news show competes with this scene.

GRANDMOTHER: Go on.

Taeo's hands rest beside his untouched rice.

Taeo looks toward Grandfather and the sibling, including both in his account.

TAEO: A gate opened at the shop on Tuesday. We all got outside. The hunters cleared it.

The sibling's spoon stops before reaching the bowl. Grandmother listens without a melodramatic hand-to-mouth pose.

TAEO: I saw a message saying I was a summoner.

No re-created gate spectacle, parents' death association or claim the gate caused awakening.

dialogue.text: A gate opened at the shop on Tuesday. We all got outside. The hunters cleared it.
I saw a message saying I was a summoner.

full_script:
Closer across sibling and Taeo. The sibling leans enough to inspect his face, as if an injury might have been overlooked.

SIBLING: Were you hurt?

TAEO: No. Nobody was.

SIBLING: Were you scared?

Taeo starts a small reassuring smile. It goes away before he answers.

TAEO: Yes.

A quiet beat with the whole table still present at the edges. Nib looks down at his own cup, leaving this answer to Taeo. No dialogue explaining his reaction.

Grandmother sets down the serving chopsticks she had picked up, still on her side of the table.

GRANDMOTHER: We spoke that evening.

TAEO: Before it happened.

GRANDMOTHER: And after?

Taeo looks at his rice bowl. This is a question, not an accusation of lying about the order of events.

Taeo rubs one thumb along his other knuckle, an ordinary anxious habit with no palm emphasis or magic cue.

TAEO: I kept thinking I'd call when I knew what to say.

GRANDMOTHER: You could've said that.

The line is plain, spoken while she looks at him. Do not isolate it as a grand wisdom quote.

dialogue.text: I kept thinking I'd call when I knew what to say.

full_script:
The sibling returns their spoon to the bowl without taking a bite.

SIBLING: I would've picked up.

Taeo turns toward them fully.

TAEO: I know. I should've called.

No instant hug or all-forgiven declaration. Give the sibling room to hear it without performing forgiveness.

Grandfather looks from Taeo to Nib, then back.

GRANDFATHER: Did you get assessed?

TAEO: I did. My output's low. We found a little connection. We still don't know how to send him back.

Short and accurate. Do not add a rank, license or implication the office declared Nib harmless. Nobody demonstrates the connection at lunch.

dialogue.text: I did. My output's low. We found a little connection. We still don't know how to send him back.

full_script:
Grandmother addresses Nib directly, her voice less certain than when addressing Taeo.

GRANDMOTHER: Is there someone you need to tell where you are?

Nib's hand rests near his water cup. He does not touch his pouch or produce the sketch.

NIB: I can't tell anyone. I don't know how to reach them.

This follows his established displacement and does not name new relatives or settle who waits for him. The family receives a real answer rather than solving him.

dialogue.text: Is there someone you need to tell where you are?
I can't tell anyone. I don't know how to reach them.

full_script:
Grandmother takes that in. She does not say he is part of their family now or promise a homecoming. Taeo watches Nib rather than answering for him.

GRANDMOTHER: I see.

A small silence. Then she takes the serving chopsticks again and indicates the platter rather than putting food in his bowl unasked.

GRANDMOTHER: Fish?

NIB: Yes. That piece.

He points to an ordinary piece within the platter, neither the largest nor a joke-sized fish.

Grandmother serves the indicated piece to Nib, then starts to add another to the sibling's bowl. The sibling slides their bowl a few centimeters away, a familiar practiced motion.

SIBLING: I already have some.

GRANDMOTHER: Then eat it.

Taeo's restrained laugh escapes. The sibling looks at him; a small corner of their mouth moves. This recalls Chapter 1 behavior without repeating its phone dialogue.

The meal finally moves. Grandfather reaches toward a side dish and asks Taeo the practical question he has been waiting to ask.

GRANDFATHER: You're still at the shop?

TAEO: Yes. I worked yesterday so I could come today.

SIBLING: Don't swap back.

TAEO: I already worked it.

The sibling resumes eating. This establishes the routine Saturday fulfillment aloud without staging another work episode. No claim of hunter wages for Taeo.

dialogue.text: Yes. I worked yesterday so I could come today.

full_script:
Nib is concentrating on separating a piece of fish with the edge of his ordinary spoon. He leaves the visible bone on the rim of his plate, successfully but without expert showmanship. Across the table, Taeo takes a proper mouthful of food. Grandmother watches him eat rather than pursuing the questions indefinitely.

No dialogue. A real breathing beat after the uncomfortable news. No healing glow, obedience or pet-feeding.

After lunch, clear short time cut. The meal table is folded upright against the north wall, dishes in the kitchen. Grandmother is there rinsing plates; Grandfather sits in his usual west-side chair with a cup. Taeo has helped carry dishes in this mundane cut, not earned a new relationship offscreen.

The sibling places the puzzle board flat on the cleared floor where the table stood. Taeo sits cross-legged at its south edge, sibling west. Nib chooses a floor cushion to the east, a little back from the board, with a cup of water on a coaster to his RIGHT, well outside the pieces. Taeo's phone remains in his hoodie pocket.

SIBLING: This bit's yours.

Their finger indicates the ragged cloud gap.

Taeo lifts one blue-white piece from the shallow sorting tray, turns it once and tries it at the gap. It does not seat. He withdraws it instead of forcing the cardboard and returns it to the tray. This is the distinct white piece with a blue upper corner that will eventually complete the cloud; it is being tried in the wrong place now.

TAEO: You left all the same-looking ones.

SIBLING: I did the roofs.

TAEO: Convenient.

A little family competitiveness. The sibling has already done substantial ordinary work; this is neither a genius puzzle nor a remedial task.

dialogue.text: You left all the same-looking ones.

full_script:
The sibling nudges the printed puzzle-box lid toward Taeo. Its image shows the completed seaside town, including the pale cloud.

SIBLING: Here. It gets wider on this side.

Taeo compares image and pieces, leaning close beside them. Nib can see the box from his separate cushion; no mistaken recognition of home.

dialogue.text: Here. It gets wider on this side.

full_script:
Nib holds his water cup in his LEFT hand and watches Taeo return to the same blue-white piece. Taeo offers it halfway toward him without pushing it into his hands.

TAEO: Want to try?

NIB: You've got the whole picture there.

SIBLING: That's not the point.

Nib gives the sibling a level look. The sibling holds it. Their different ideas of a useful activity are allowed to be funny without either becoming foolish.

dialogue.text: You've got the whole picture there.

full_script:
Nib puts down his cup on the safe coaster, leans forward from the cushion and takes the offered piece in his RIGHT hand. Taeo withdraws his now-empty hand. Nib tries the piece along the cloud edge. It does not fit; he rotates it, and it still does not fit.

NIB: No.

SIBLING: That's what he said last time.

TAEO: I heard that.

The joke is familiar sibling teasing, not Nib's inability to understand a simple game. No scout superpower solves it.

dialogue.text: That's what he said last time.

full_script:
Nib puts the unsuccessful piece back in the shallow sorting tray and settles back on his cushion. Taeo leans farther over the board, tugging his hoodie pocket against his leg. The phone shifts uncomfortably inside it. He takes it out. Habit carries his thumb toward the screen before he has decided what to check; the display faces him and is not shown.

The sibling's gaze follows the movement and holds on the phone. No vibration, notification, pending emergency or new message is shown.

Taeo notices the sibling looking at it. He does not start a speech. He sets the phone screen-down behind his RIGHT hip, still within reach and well clear of the board and water, and turns back to the puzzle-box image.

TAEO: Show me which side gets wider.

The sibling points again, more precisely. Taeo leans in to see. His choice is sustained attention, not switching off the outside world forever.

dialogue.text: Show me which side gets wider.

full_script:
Close over their shoulders. The sibling slides two OTHER loose pieces together on the tray, making a small patch of cloud. Taeo draws the tray closer to the gap, keeping it flat on the floor, and compares the cluster against the outline.

SIBLING: Turn it.

TAEO: This way?

SIBLING: The other way.

Ordinary collaboration, not a climactic tactical instruction. No magic sensation or remembered course overlay.

Taeo turns the cluster on the tray rather than lifting fragile joined pieces unsupported, then moves its two pieces individually into the matching gap. The sibling presses their own fingertip lightly on the board edge to steady it. Both pieces settle correctly.

SFX: tik.

TAEO: There.

SIBLING: One more.

A single remaining white notch interrupts the cloud. The wider blue sky remains unfinished.

They search the remaining loose pieces together. Nib, still seated east of the board, is looking at the piece he tried earlier in the shallow sorting tray. He points, without touching anyone's hand.

NIB: That one again.

The sibling lifts it, compares its shape to the now-obvious notch, and turns it a quarter turn. It is a visible fit anyone can confirm, not a perfect deduction from an upside-down image.

The sibling holds the piece toward Taeo. He accepts it, looking from the piece to the sibling.

SIBLING: Your bit.

Taeo sets the piece into the notch. The cloud is complete. Their earlier promise has a small visible result; most of the puzzle remains to do.

No speech from Taeo. Let his small pleased expression and the sibling's release of tension carry the payoff.

Grandmother appears at the kitchen edge with the opened packet of spicy seaweed from the grocery bag, held over a clean plate. Taeo and the sibling look up from the finished cloud section; Nib turns from his cushion.

GRANDMOTHER: Away from the pieces.

SIBLING: We know.

They move their hands back from the board before taking any food. One ordinary boundary keeps the warmth lived-in rather than ceremonious.

A little later, the snack plate rests on the low cabinet, not over the puzzle. The sibling has taken one sheet and Taeo another; Nib has his water. Taeo looks at the unfinished blue sky, then at the sibling.

TAEO: Want to do another bit?

SIBLING: You're not going?

TAEO: Not yet.

No impossible permanent promise, new appointment or hint that Nib has replaced his own home. Taeo is choosing how to spend this actual afternoon.

Final broad, quiet view of the room. Taeo and the sibling set their snacks down on the cabinet plate and return to the board. Taeo reaches into the loose-piece tray at the same time as the sibling; they adjust naturally to avoid bumping hands. Nib remains on the east cushion, drinking water and watching for his own interest. Grandfather has leaned a little farther forward with his cup, staying in the west chair rather than joining a sentimental circle. Grandmother returns to her kitchen task.

Taeo's phone is still screen-down behind his right hip. His jacket waits on the hook; the front door is closed. No departure countdown. The finished pale cloud is visible amid the still-unfinished sky.

No dialogue, inner monologue, new threat, mystery clue, System window or reward. End on time actually spent together.
